mission: Test whether only PREVIOUS calendar week outcomes can estimate when an early sale has greater *incremental monetary value* than continued trade at first 0.5/3 RTH hour, using fixed low-capacity model.
source: Existing private Terminal 5m RTH snapshots and v21 matched force-vs-hold differences; no new market data collected
features_from_completed5m: net five minute close gain since entry pct
closing position in observed high-low range (0..1)
mean 12 prior observed 5m high-low ranges as pct of entry
predictand: force early close at next observed 5m open net minus matched original 52-RTH-hour hold net, in percentage points. This is NOT a prediction of trade direction or a live training signal.
model: single fixed ordinary ridge regression: intercept+6 z-scored features; L2 penalty 12 per standardized feature, zero intercept penalty; labels clipped to +/-10 pp ONLY while training; no hyperparameter search.
admission: A test market week is permitted when at least 20 previous eligible events across at least 6 distinct previous market weeks exist; other entries are no-forecast, kept in denominators; same-week events never train each other.
decision: sell remainder at designated checkpoint only if predicted incremental net return > 0.25 percentage points; otherwise continue baseline; cost differences are already included in labels. Predicted score is derived from prior weeks only.
controls: At checkpoint sell if completed 5m close below original entry
Perfect future oracle max(delta,0) only for theoretical upper bound, not tradeable
primary_metric: Paired mean incremental net return PER ORIGINAL PARENT episode on weeks when model is active, compare to hold and naive below-entry policy using same episodes.
secondary_metrics: source coverage and unforecastable early weeks
realized total per original across all original market weeks with no action in warmup
rule: Do not tune threshold or ridge penalty after viewing results; no model-derived position sizing. Published code is research only.
data_rights: No licensed raw prices or proprietary event quotes published. point-in-time/source adjustment not verified.
